title: Table partitioning and data lifecycle
brief: Use table partitions for a useful pruning or lifecycle boundary without assuming they distribute work.
outcomes: Account for uniqueness, references and safe retention
entry: Typed time, indexes and history requirements.

heading.title: A boundary in the table
heading.brief: Place proposed dated class sessions in monthly partitions; distinguish the logical table, children and physical server placement.

heading.title: Pruning and access paths
heading.brief: Follow predicates into selected partitions and local indexes; show when an expression or broad date range still touches many partitions.

heading.title: Keys across partitions
heading.brief: Work through session identity and referenced bookings; explain engine-specific uniqueness limits rather than promising a global index.

heading.title: Retention as a change
heading.brief: Detach or drop an expired period only after references, history, readers and recovery requirements are resolved; include partition creation and skew costs.
